title: Waking up after anesthesia
what: After surgery you are taken to the recovery room. There you wake up under the watch of nurses and a doctor.
why: After any operation or procedure under general anesthesia or sedation.
duration: usually 30 minutes to 2 hours, then you are moved to a ward or go home
tell_doctor: If you had severe nausea after anesthesia before
If you have been confused after anesthesia
Whether you need your glasses or hearing aid right after waking

prepare.title: In advance
prepare.text: Ask how long you will stay in the recovery room and when your family can see you.

prepare.title: Going home
prepare.text: If it is day surgery, arrange for someone to pick you up and stay with you for the first day.

bring: Glasses, hearing aid: give them to the staff
steps: You wake up with sensors on you and an oxygen mask or tubes
A nurse asks how you are and watches your blood pressure and breathing
If you are in pain or feel sick, say so and you will be given medicine
When you are awake and all is well, you are moved to a ward or prepared for discharge
feel: A dry mouth, sometimes a scratchy throat
You may not remember the first hours. This is normal
after: Get up for the first time only with help from staff
Drinking and eating start when the doctor allows
For a day after anesthesia, do not drive and do not make important decisions
red_flags: Trouble breathing or chest pain: tell the nurse at once
At home: extreme drowsiness, cannot be woken: call your local emergency number

faq.q: Why am I shivering after anesthesia?
faq.a: This happens because of the medicines and the cool operating room. You will be covered and warmed.

faq.q: When can my relatives come in?
faq.a: Usually after you are moved to a ward. Rules differ, so ask the clinic.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Arrange for someone to meet you afterward. Food and water only until the time the clinic gave you.
